Based on the document provided, I can identify the following operative rental housing obligations as of October 1, 2026:

## Rent Increases (AB 1482)

**Obligation - Rent Cap:**

citations.cited_text:
When Can Rent Be Increased Under State Law AB1482
The JCO does not regulate rent increases, however, state law
AB 1482, the California Tenant Protection Act of 2019
,
may regulate the rent amount in buildings that are older than 15 years old.

content.text: State law AB 1482, the California Tenant Protection Act of 2019, may regulate the rent amount in buildings that are older than 15 years old.

citations.cited_text:
Effective August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025, the maximum allowable increase is
8.9%
.

content.text: Effective August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025, the maximum allowable increase is 8.9%.

citations.cited_text:
(
A
nnual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower).

content.text: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower.
**Exemptions from Rent Caps:**

citations.cited_text:
Properties
not
covered under AB 1482:
-Units that were constructed within the last 15 years (this applies on a rolling basis – i.e.. a unit constructed on January 1, 2006 is not covered as of January, 1 2020, but is covered on and after January 1, 2021).

content.text: Units that were constructed within the last 15 years are not covered.

citations.cited_text: -Units restricted by a deed, regulatory restrictions, or other recorded document limiting the affordability to low or moderate-income households.

content.text: Units restricted by a deed, regulatory restrictions, or other recorded document limiting the affordability to low or moderate-income households are exempt.

citations.cited_text: -A two-unit property, provided the second unit was occupied by an owner of the property for the entire period of the tenancy.

content.text: A two-unit property, provided the second unit was occupied by an owner of the property for the entire period of the tenancy, is exempt.

citations.cited_text: -Units that are already subject to the City’s RSO.

content.text: Units that are already subject to the City's RSO are exempt.

## Just Cause Eviction

**Obligation:**

citations.cited_text: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

content.text: The ordinance prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

citations.cited_text: In order to apply to a tenancy, it requires that the tenant either has lived in the same unit for at least six months or that their original lease expired, whichever comes first.

content.text: In order to apply to a tenancy, it requires that the tenant either has lived in the same unit for at least six months or that their original lease expired, whichever comes first.
**Eviction for Non-Payment:**

citations.cited_text: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

content.text: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
**At-Fault Eviction Reasons (no relocation assistance required):**

citations.cited_text:
Failure to pay rent
Failure to cure a violation of the rental agreement
Creating a nuisance or causing damage to the property
Using the rental unit for an illegal purpose
Failure to renew a similar rental agreement
Failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit
The person at the end of the lease term is a subtenant not approved by the landlord
Tenant is not at-fault
Situations in which the property owner wishes to regain the use of the rental unit, as the result of a personal or business decision, and
not the
tenant’s fault, may be cause for eviction, but the property owner may have to pay the tenant
relocation assistance
.

content.text: Reasons include failure to pay rent, failure to cure a violation of the rental agreement, creating a nuisance or causing damage to the property, using the rental unit for an illegal purpose, failure to renew a similar rental agreement, failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit, and the person at the end of the lease term being a subtenant not approved by the landlord.

content.text: These reasons include the owner or an immediate family member moving into the rental unit, resident manager moving into the rental unit when required by law or by an affordable housing covenant or regulatory agreement, demolition, permanent removal from the rental market, or conversion to non-residential, government order to vacate, HUD owns and is selling the property, residential hotel being converted or demolished, and conversion to affordable housing.

**Obligation:**

These reasons include
The
owner or an immediate family member
will move into the rental unit

Required Registration and Posted Notification
All properties rented or offered for rent must be
registered annually
.

content.text: All properties rented or offered for rent must be registered annually.

citations.cited_text: Once registration is complete, the landlord will receive a Registration Certificate (Statement) which must be displayed in a conspicuous place on the property or served to the tenant.

content.text: Once registration is complete, the landlord will receive a Registration Certificate (Statement) which must be displayed in a conspicuous place on the property or served to the tenant.

citations.cited_text:
Beginning August 20, 2025, landlords must post a
Notice of Right to Counsel
in a conspicuous common area of the residential building where the tenant resides.

content.text: Beginning August 20, 2025, landlords must post a Notice of Right to Counsel in a conspicuous common area of the residential building where the tenant resides.

citations.cited_text: All landlords of residential properties must provide a Notice of Renters’ Protections to tenants who begin or renew their tenancy on or after January 27, 2023.

content.text: All landlords of residential properties must provide a Notice of Renters' Protections to tenants who begin or renew their tenancy on or after January 27, 2023.
**Eviction Notice Filing:**

citations.cited_text:
Eviction Notices Filed with LAHD
Applies to all JCO & RSO rental properties – All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.

content.text: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
